title.narrative: Emergency need assessments in Punia (Maniema) and Beni (North Kivu) for ECHO HIP 2017 in DRC

description.narrative: While it appears to be stable, particularly due to a weak presence of humanitarian actors who could regularly alert on the situation on the ground, the Maniema Province continues to face an alarming humanitarian situation which needs more particular attention. In addition, Maniema continues to be affected by effects of armed conflicts and various atrocities caused by several armed groups (May-May and Raia Mutomboke) very active in the neighbouring territories of North and South Kivu, pushing thousands of families to displace to Maniema, in the territories bordering North or South Kivu (such as Punia, Pangi and Kabambare). CAFOD is currently providing emergency response with its partner BDD Kasongo in two territories (Pangi in Maniema and Shabunda in South Kivu) with funding obtained from ECHO in 2016. Similarly, the humanitarian situation remains critical in Beni (North Kivu) where people continue moving massively as a result of cruel and killings of civilians by alleged Ugandan rebels of ADF/NALU. After a quick emergency intervention co-funded with Caritas Australia, CAFOD, received another small START Network funding which helped to meet priority needs of some households affected by these atrocities in this area without being able to cover the bulk of humanitarian needs. Therefore, CAFOD would like to organize needs assessments in both zones to facilitate the development of new proposals for institutional funds applications to be submitted to ECHO under the HIP 2017, to enable us pursue the humanitarian work and cover the remaining needs in these targeted areas of Maniema, South and North Kivu. The current operational project funds will allow to hire consultants who will carry out need assessments of good of high quality as required by the donor (ECHO)
